title: Leaders Obsessed With Excellence Can Become Monsters
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This article examines how an admirable pursuit of excellence can curdle into mistreatment of others when leaders demand the same intensity from everyone and punish those who can't sustain it. It describes the pattern of team turnover this creates, along with the self-justifying language such leaders use to describe their own harshness, quoting several boastful phrases used to excuse cruelty in the name of standards. The piece notes this affliction isn't confined to any particular industry, appearing across founders, chefs, coaches, and nonprofit leaders alike, and closes by insisting good people never let that obsession win.
points: An obsession with excellence can turn otherwise normal leaders into harsh, mistreating bosses.
Such leaders often use self-justifying, boastful language to excuse their intensity and cruelty.
The resulting team turnover is described as a revolving door despite initial outside appeal.
The pattern is said to appear across industries and roles, not confined to any one type of enterprise.
quotes: Ordinarily normal people who become obsessed with creating excellence often become monsters along the way.
Their relentless pursuit of excellence allows them to justify whatever actions they deem necessary to accomplish it with the highest quality.
The team becomes a revolving door for talent. From the outside, the passion and dedication can appear alluring to some, but once on the inside, most retreat.
When one well-known leader was named by a magazine as the second meanest boss in a city, they complained about not being first.
The pursuit of excellence is a virtuous endeavor. But when it becomes an obsession, it can turn angels into demons.
